On a point of order, the hon. Minister of Agriculture.

speakerposition: Deputy Prime Minister; Minister of Agriculture; Vice-President; President of the Privy Council
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I am advised that when you called the question on Motion No. 5, I was involved in a bit of an exchange with the hon. member for Broadview-Greenwood, and that there may have been a misinterpretation on the position that was expressed on this side of the House in that we were opposed to this particular motion. I wonder if you would seek the unanimous consent of the House to go back to the consideration of Motion No. 5 so that the question might be more appropriately put.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
speechtext: Is there unanimous consent?
Agreed.
No.

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
speechtext: There is not unanimous consent.

speakerposition: Deputy Prime Minister; Minister of Agriculture; Vice-President; President of the Privy Council
speechtext:
Since opposition members have won that round, because they have refused to give unanimous consent to go back, perhaps we could agree to move on to third reading. I think that that is a very major concession that has been granted and it might help us in facilitating the passage of this bill.
I want to repeat to hon. members the points that have been made across the way on the motion that has been proposed by the hon. member for Algoma. I say again that I have a lot of sympathy and it has a lot of merit. Again, I went out to make doubly sure and our Justice officials have indicated and advised us that there clearly would be jurisdictional problems with the motion that is being proposed as it relates to the relationship between the federal and provincial governments.
I want to make it very clear that the only reason that we on this side of the House are taking that position is strictly on the advice of our Justice officials. I think that we will be able to achieve the ultimate objective and really put into effect what the hon. member is proposing here in a different way. I wanted to make that clearly understood by all hon. members. Perhaps with those kind words, we could proceed to third reading.

March 14, 1990
Government Orders

speakerposition: Deputy Chair of Committees of the Whole
speechtext:
The House will now proceed to the taking of the deferred division at the report stage of the bill now before the House.
Shall I call in the members?

Mr. Speaker, while I was interested in the hon. minister's comments on the point of order that he raised, the consultations that have been taking place are along the line that we would defer the division with regard to motion No. 10 and the report stage vote until tomorrow afternoon. I believe the consultations that have taken place are along that line.
In view of that, I understand that the government is disposed to call it six o'clock. If that were the decision, that would save calling in the members today, because I understand there will be an opposition motion tomorrow which would involve an agreement. The House Leaders have been discussing this and have been expecting that third reading would be debated next Monday. I may be wrong. There may be other consultations, but that is my understanding of the arrangement.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada; Parliamentary Secretary to the Leader of the Government in the House of Commons
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, part of the problem we are having here is that this has erupted in the last couple of minutes. I have had conversations with members on the other side of the House. I have not been able to have conversations with my own party Whip to confirm his understanding of votes. I would think that with the accommodation that has existed within the House today, perhaps we could pass report stage on division and go from there.
Mr. Speaker, my understanding is that the arrangement was that we would defer the division until tomorrow on report stage and that we would go to third reading next Monday on this bill.

speakerposition: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada; Parliamentary Secretary to the Leader of the Government in the House of Commons
speechtext:
I am sorry to cause confusion and difficulty for the Chair. Perhaps the Chair could give us a couple
of minutes because we do want to make sure that there is co-operation between the three parties, which is clearly the intention at this moment. We just had to get the right players together. If we could have a couple of minutes that will allow us to resolve it.

Mr. Speaker, there have been discussions between the parties and I think you will find there is agreement that the questions would be put and we will deal with them when they are put. I understand the questions will be disposed of without the necessity of a vote. Assuming report stage of the bill is adopted, as I am sure it will be, we will then adjourn.
In other words, Mr. Speaker, we do not want you to put the yeas and nays on the division.
